root_cause.text: In the Qdisc-less transmit path, the return code from dev_hard_start_xmit for a GSO-segmented skb list is interpreted by TCP as complete failure (even when only some segments were dropped), causing TCP to not advance snd_nxt and leading to a retransmission deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check for `is_list` (indicating GSO segmentation) and overrides the return code to `NETDEV_TX_OK` in that case, with the comment: "GSO segments a single SKB into a list of frames. TCP expects error to mean none of the data was sent." The CVE description details the failure mode where a single lost segment in a GSO super frame results in TCP rejecting valid ACKs and stalling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a boolean variable `is_list` to support upcoming code restructuring or new feature related to transmit queue handling.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration `bool is_list = false;` inside the `if (READ_ONCE(txq->xmit_lock_owner) != cpu)` block.
intent_record.how: The change introduces an unused boolean variable at this point; no runtime behavior change occurs, but it prepares for future use that may affect queueing logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TCP error semantics for GSO by treating partial segment send as success and properly handling non-GSO residual errors.
intent_record.what: In __dev_queue_xmit, after calling dev_hard_start_xmit, the diff adds a check for is_list (skb->next != NULL) before the call, then overrides rc to NETDEV_TX_OK if is_list is true; moves HARD_TX_UNLOCK outside the if block; adds a check for !skb after unlock to goto out on completion; and adds a condition that if not is_list, sets rc to -ENETDOWN after the critical message.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that for GSO (segmented) skbs, any error returned by dev_hard_start_xmit is ignored and treated as success (NETDEV_TX_OK), preventing TCP from misinterpreting partial send failures as complete failures. For single skbs, a residual error (e.g., NETDEV_TX_BUSY) now results in rc = -ENETDOWN, causing the packet to be dropped and reported as an error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix erroneous -ENETDOWN return by moving the assignment inside the recursion_alert conditional block.
intent_record.what: Moved the assignment `rc = -ENETDOWN;` from outside the recursion_alert code block to inside it, so it is only executed when the dead loop condition is triggered.
intent_record.how: Before: `rc` was always set to -ENETDOWN after the recursion_alert label, regardless of whether the dead loop was detected. After: `rc` is set to -ENETDOWN only within the recursion_alert block, preventing the function from erroneously returning -ENETDOWN when the loop condition is not met.
